**"AWS is shutting down Mechanical Turk, which let humans beat AI at certain work tasks"**

Amazon has announced it will shut down its Mechanical Turk (MTurk) platform on September 30, 2026. Launched in 2005, MTurk enabled companies to outsource small, routine digital tasks to human workers, particularly those tasks that computers initially struggled with, such as labeling data, tagging images, and transcribing audio. At its peak, the platform connected over 500,000 workers, known as "turkers," and played a key role in labeling data for Amazon’s SageMaker AI service. However, rapid advancements in artificial intelligence have rendered many of these tasks more efficiently managed by machines, leading to a steady decline in MTurk’s relevance. Worker advocates, including Turkopticon's Krista Pawloski, noted that Amazon had deprioritized the platform in recent years, even as competitors like Scale AI and Prolific emerged. The closure signals a broader shift in AI economics, where automated systems are increasingly surpassing human capabilities in data processing. Despite MTurk’s shutdown, Amazon affirms its ongoing commitment to serving its AWS and retail customers. The move has left some long-term workers scrambling to find alternative platforms, especially as certain businesses still depend on human task outsourcing. ([techradar.com](https://www.techradar.com/pro/aws-is-shutting-down-mechanical-turk-which-let-humans-beat-ai-at-certain-work-tasks?utm_source=openai))
